# waroom_runbook (Resource)

Manages a Waroom runbook. A runbook is Markdown content identified by its path-style namespace (e.g. `/default`, `/api-server/recovery`).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Write the Markdown content inline with a heredoc.
resource "waroom_runbook" "inline" {
  namespace = "/api-server/recovery"
  blob      = <<-EOT
    # API server recovery

    1. Check the error rate on the dashboard.
    2. Restart the API server.
    3. Confirm the error rate is back to normal.
  EOT
}

# Or read it from a Markdown file placed next to this configuration.
resource "waroom_runbook" "from_file" {
  namespace = "/database/failover"
  blob      = file("${path.module}/runbook.md")
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `blob` (String) Markdown content of the runbook. An empty string is not allowed.
- `namespace` (String) The path-style namespace of the runbook, e.g. `/api-server/recovery`. It must start with `/`, may contain only ASCII letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `/`, and is at most 255 characters. The root namespace `/` is not supported. Changing it renames the runbook in place.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) The time the runbook was created, in RFC 3339 format.
- `id` (String) Runbook ID. This is an alias for `namespace`.
- `updated_at` (String) The time the runbook was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Runbooks can be imported by specifying the runbook namespace
import {
  to = waroom_runbook.inline
  id = "/api-server/recovery"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Runbooks can be imported by specifying the runbook namespace
terraform import waroom_runbook.inline /api-server/recovery
```
